task_statement:
Research question (as posed on 2026-10-06, in the area of defensive suppression and counter strategy (best/avoid)):
A defense's effect on opponents' H2-H1 change is a reliable team trait.

Data available on that date:
- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13; partial before)
- NBA 2025-26 playoffs (complete from 2026-06-21; partial before)
- Sources: Per-game files from the NBA stats API: play-by-play (action type, sub-type, clock, period, score, player, shot distance and result), substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes and partial possessions, box-score summary. Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database built from the play-by-play.
- Units available to a study of this question (as recorded): 120 team-seasons

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.

research_concepts: H2-H1 change in opponent points per possession (second half minus first half)
temporal stability (year-to-year reliability) of team effects
counter strategy (best/avoid) as a related context
methodological_questions: Is the team-level defensive effect on opponents' H2-H1 change stable across seasons (test-retest reliability over 2022-23 to 2025-26)?
Can a defensive H2-H1 effect be estimated reliably from one team-season of roughly 82 games, given its noise?
Do game-script, score-margin, pace, and opponent-quality confounders produce the H2-H1 pattern without a defensive trait?
Do free-throw or other mechanical possessions inflate H2-H1 contrasts?
What reliability threshold would count as a 'reliable team trait' under a pre-registered rule?

historical_evidence.finding: Split-half reliability of connector teammate-path quality Q_p on 102 connectors: r=+0.215, Spearman-Brown 0.355, ICC 0.216, with 78.4% of variance within player. [prior work] concludes that Q_p is too unreliable to treat as a stable scoutable trait; the mechanism is recorded as A_unanswerable and the limit as low measurement reliability.

Playsheet counter ranking tested in 10 completed 2025-26 playoff series, 665 counter observations, averaging 6.9 possessions per counter. Full-rank Spearman was not significant (rho -0.0639, p=0.099717). A pairwise BEST>AVOID difference was reported (p=0.004018). [prior work] flags leakage risk from season_cap_yy=26 and low measurement reliability.

Opponent PPP after a star's second Q1/Q2 foul: the raw lag-1 effect of +0.204 came from free-throw possessions (41.8% of treated vs 9.9% of controls). Excluding free-throw trips, lag-1 was +0.0486 (CI -0.0060 to +0.0991, perm p=0.0655), and no lag cleared the pre-specified bars.

On 120 team-seasons, the Possession Control Index gained dR2 +0.139 over ORtg for Net Rating, but the gain came from a leakage term correlated with DRtg (+0.894). Offensive-control components added only +0.005. [prior work] notes that Net Rating contains DRtg by construction, so defense-correlated features leak into defensive outcomes.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Treating a per-player teammate-path quality metric as a stable trait, assessed by split-half reliability
failed_approaches.why: Split-half r=0.215 (Spearman-Brown 0.355) and ICC 0.216, with most variance within player across halves. Recorded as too low for a stable trait; mechanism A_unanswerable, limited by low measurement reliability.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Validating a ranked counter strategy with a Spearman full-rank test over playoff series
failed_approaches.why: Average of about 6.9 possessions per counter is too few. Full-rank signal was null (rho -0.0639). Recorded as inconclusive, with leakage from season_cap_yy=26 and low measurement reliability flagged.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Counting free-throw trips as ordinary opponent possessions after a foul event
failed_approaches.why: Mechanical free-throw trips produced an apparent +0.204 lag-1 effect; apples-to-apples result was +0.049 and not significant. Recorded as artifact, mechanism C_artifact, limited by confounding.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Adding a defense-correlated index to explain Net Rating
failed_approaches.why: The headline dR2 +0.139 was a DRtg-tracking leakage term (corr +0.894); offensive controls added only +0.005. Recorded as artifact, mechanism C_artifact, limited by leakage.

evidence_establishes: In this project's [prior work], low split-half reliability (SF-[prior work]) and small per-counter possession counts (SF-[prior work]) have each blocked stable-trait claims in closely related player and counter settings.
Mechanical possession types (free throws, [prior work]) and defense-correlated features (SF-[prior work]) have each produced spurious effects, so the H2-H1 test needs explicit controls.
A 120 team-season unit set (SF-[prior work] notes n=120) is the same size as the proposed sample, so [prior work] indicates the scale of prior team-season tests.
evidence_does_not_establish: No retrieved record tests defensive H2-H1 change directly. None reports a team-level H2-H1 reliability estimate.
No record gives the test-retest correlation of any team defensive quantity across seasons.
No record shows whether 2022-23 to 2025-26 data have rule or pace drift that would affect H2-H1 comparability.
The retrieved records do not establish the outcome of this question; the evidence is analogous, not direct.
own_inferences: Each team-season has about 41 games per half, so the H2-H1 contrast per team-season is noisier than full-season defensive ratings. Reliability is likely to be lower than for full-season DRtg.
With 120 team-seasons (about 90 consecutive-season pairs), detecting a true test-retest r near 0.3 is feasible. Detecting r near 0.15 would not be.
Score margin and garbage-time effects plausibly drive H2-H1 contrasts, so a naive H2-H1 difference could reflect game script rather than defense.
Defensive ratings contain the defense by construction, so any predictor built from opponent scoring leaks into the outcome.
uncertainties: Whether the H2-H1 metric has been computed in the project before. No record for it was returned.
The exact definition of H2-H1 (by possessions, by points, or by minutes) and how overtime is handled.
Whether playoff data is comparable to regular season data for this contrast.
The distribution of within-team H2-H1 variance, which determines power. It is not in the retrieved records.
Whether the prior-record pipelines (season_cap_yy=26) apply to this question.

historical_effect.explanation: The retrieved records do not answer the question, so they did not change the bottom-line decision to test it. They did change the design. The low-reliability result (SF-[prior work]) moved the design to a test-retest reliability estimate with a pre-set threshold instead of assuming a trait. The artifact records ([prior work], SF-[prior work]) required excluding mechanical possessions and defense-correlated predictors. The small-sample null (SF-[prior work]) led to using team-season units rather than per-counter units.

blocking_constraints.text: Single team-season H2-H1 contrasts are noisy; reliability may be too low to call the effect a trait, as SF-[prior work] found for a different metric.
120 team-seasons gives about 90 consecutive-season pairs, enough only for moderate reliability (about r≥0.3). Smaller true reliability cannot be detected.
Score margin, garbage time, pace, and opponent quality can produce H2-H1 differences without any defensive trait.

prior_work.summary: No retrieved record tests whether defensive H2-H1 change is a reliable team trait. Related records show low reliability of a player-level metric, small-sample failure of counter rankings, and artifact effects from free throws and defense-correlated predictors. These are cautions for this test, not answers to it.

risks.text: Team-season H2-H1 contrast may have low test-retest reliability, as in SF-[prior work].
With 120 team-seasons, only moderate reliability is detectable; a null may reflect low power.
Score margin, garbage time, and pace drive H2-H1 contrasts; opponent quality must be adjusted.
Most teams may have H2-H1 near zero, so the between-team variance is small relative to noise.
Per-half possession counts per team-season are modest, so the H2-H1 estimate per team is noisy.
Free-throw and foul-driven trips can enter H2-H1 mechanically, as in [prior work].
Using defensive outcomes to define the trait, or playoff data from later rounds, can leak the outcome into the predictor, as in SF-[prior work] and SF-[prior work].
Multiple H2-H1 definitions, windows, and splits invite selective reporting.
Rule, pace, and roster changes across 2022-23 to 2025-26 may alter H2-H1 comparability.
Placebo tests on shuffled team labels or on first-half-only contrasts are needed to separate a trait from noise.

design.estimand: Test-retest correlation of team-level defensive H2-H1 effect (opponent PPP in second half minus first half, adjusted for score margin, pace, and opponent quality) across consecutive regular seasons, with shrinkage-based reliability.
design.unit: Team-season (one defense in one regular season).
design.sample: 30 teams x 4 regular seasons (2022-23 to 2025-26) = 120 team-seasons; about 90 consecutive-season pairs. Exclude garbage-time possessions and overtime. Playoffs reported as secondary only.
design.power: Detect a true reliability of r≥0.30 at alpha 0.05 with 80% power (about 85 pairs). Report the confidence interval. Note that r near 0.15 is not detectable and a null at that level is uninformative.
design.controls: Adjust for average score margin per half, pace, opponent offensive quality, and home/away. Exclude free-throw and foul-driven possessions, following [prior work]. Do not use any defensive rating in the predictor, following SF-[prior work]. Use only data available before the outcome season.
design.falsification: Placebo: shuffle team labels within season and recompute the correlation. Also compare first-half-only contrasts for the same pairs. Both must show no reliability; if they do, the effect is not a trait.
design.multiplicity: Pre-register a single primary definition of H2-H1 and one primary reliability statistic. Report alternative windows and splits as exploratory, with Bonferroni or Holm correction.
design.decision_rule: Call the defensive H2-H1 effect a reliable team trait only if the primary cross-season correlation is at least 0.30 with a 95% CI excluding 0, survives the score-margin and pace adjustments, and the placebo correlations are near zero. Call it rejected if the correlation CI excludes values of 0.30 and is near 0 after adjustment. Otherwise report it as uncertain.
design.data_version: Data snapshot as of 2026-10-06: 2022-23 to 2024-25 regular seasons and playoffs, 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13). Playoff 2025-26 is complete from 2026-06-21 and is used only as a secondary check. Freeze the data version and log the pipeline version.
